headlines.title: Woman struck by car driven by young boys in Oakland stabilized, friend says
headlines.description: A woman who was critically injured when she was struck by a car driven by two young children in Oakland has been stabilized at the hospital, a close friend said Friday. The collision happened at about 9:30 a.m. Thursday in the area of 35th and Mangels avenues, not far from Interstate 580, according to police. Security video captured a white Toyota, driven by two boys, who sources said are 6 and 4 years old, zoom by and out of frame toward Kiara Bowling and the dog. The Toyota struck another car before veering into Bowling and the dog and then crashing into a wall and fence. Bowling was taken to the hospital in critical condition, but her good friend, Jyorti Arora, provided a positive update on Friday. “I know we’re not out of the woods yet, but we all have a lot of faith,” Arora said. “She’s an incredibly strong woman, so we’re very grateful that all of her vitals are stable.” On Friday evening, Bowling’s aunt Karon Markham, who was part of the people who went to visit Bowling at Highland Hospital, added that “Kiara has a long road ahead of her. A lot of trauma to the brain, she has bleeding on the brain, she has fractures on her face and a fractured rib.” Bowling was caring for and walking Arora’s dog, Grizzly, when they were hit, Arora said. Grizzly was back home Friday after being treated for multiple injuries at an Oakland animal hospital. Her brother points out they are all still trying to recover from other family tragedies. “It’s been hard on all of us, because we recently had deaths over the recent years. The last two, regarding our mom and our brother. So, this on top of that, it’s had a huge impact on our family. So, we’re just hanging in there pulling through,” Donny, Bowling’s brother, said. Oakland Aug 6 Oakland 16 hours ago Some people quickly called for parental accountability following the crash. “These parents need to be held responsible,” witness Lavelle Shah-Marquis said. “That was my main concern. These parents need to be held responsible.” It’s a unique legal question in a case involving drivers who are barely school-age and likely far too young to even face juvenile courts. “This is such a one-off,” legal analyst Steven Clark said. “I’ve never seen anything like this in my practice of 40 years.” Clark said the case may end up being handled by social services investigations and civil courts, not criminal courts. “There will be a level of accountability here civilly,” Clark said. “Certainly the insurance will likely step in and provide coverage for this tragic accident. A lot of questions are still left to be answered.” Clark said police likely will conduct interviews to see if there was a pattern of behavior not being addressed by the parents or if they were negligent in any way. Police said the parents were cooperating with their investigation. Arora said Bowling, if she could, would likely be an advocate for the two children. “She would advocate for their safety, wherever they are going to be the most safe,” Arora said. “That’s what she would advocate for. I know that in no part of her heart would she ever wish ill on them.” According to public records, Bowling is a noted community advocate for current and former foster kids in the East Bay and a winner of multiple Bay Area pageants. She was also an outstanding student at Cal State University East Bay.

headlines.title: ‘Magic baby': Smallest surviving baby born at a Walnut Creek hospital goes home
headlines.description: On Friday, the smallest surviving baby born at a Walnut Creek hospital finally went home with her family after a rough start in life. Weighing in at less than a pound, Baby Meadow is the smallest surviving baby born at John Muir Health’s Walnut Creek Medical Center. “Even saying a miracle seems like downplayed, she’s more than a miracle and I don’t really know the word for it yet, but it’s kind of like magic. She’s just a magic baby,” said her mother, Noel Creamer. Weighing just 350 grams, Meadow is the smallest surviving baby ever born at John Muir Health in Walnut Creek. She was so tiny, her outer layer of skin hadn’t yet developed so she was a different color and her eyes were fused closed. “It was almost like seeing a kitten, because kittens are born with their eyes closed. So, I kind of call her my little kitten,” Creamer said. Creamer says her baby had a condition that prevented her from getting the nutrients she needed while in the womb. The baby was so tiny Creamer says she was told by doctors at other medical facilities she had no chance at survival. “Even though she was so small, I felt her kick and move. And I just knew I knew she didn’t make it this far along for it just to be over,” Creamer said. That’s when she turned to doctors at John Muir Health, who said they had the technology and expertise to give her a fighting chance. After 167 days, mom got the green light to take Meadow home. The staff that’s cared for her for all these weeks lined up to celebrate and say goodbye to their tiniest patient ever. Her mom says she has lots of plans for her little girl, who until now hasn’t ventured outside. “I plan on taking her camping, that’s one of the first things we’ll do,” Creamer said.

headlines.title: Tens of thousands head to San Francisco for the 18th year of Outside Lands
headlines.description: San Francisco’s Outside Lands Music Festival kicked off its 18th year on Friday with the first day of the three day music festival. Friday was headlined by British pop star Charli XCX. Fans made their way by the tnes of thousands to see Charli XCX and the many other artists spread out across the festival’s seven stages. Organizers said this year’s event at Golden Gate Park was sold out. This festival is a test of the city’s transportation systems following major traffic issues on the Fourth of July that left people traveling by transit, rideshare, robotaxi, and car stranded for hours. The city urged people not to drive to the festival or park in nearby city streets. Instead, they encouraged fans to take special SFMTA shuttles straight to the festival entrance or the Judah Muni line which is walking distance from Golden Gate Park. The city also recommends attendees walk, bike, take e-bikes or scooters, or get a ride. There are designated rideshare drop-off and pick-up spots near the festival and Waymo rides are available in an area a few blocks away from the event. Traffic in the Richmond District following the festival Friday was slow but still moved forward, with crowds of attendees walking home and many using e-bikes and scooters to make their way through the city.

headlines.title: Federal court blocks Trump administration's new rules for homelessness funding
headlines.description: A Bay Area county says it has scored a legal victory in its lawsuit against the Trump administration, adding that Friday’s court ruling could help keep thousands of formerly homeless people housed, including children and older adults. The Trump administration previously announced new rules for how $4 billion in federal funding could be spent to combat homelessness across the country. But nonprofits and local governments — including Santa Clara County — argued those new restrictions would lead to dramatic cuts in funding for permanent housing, so they sued HUD. Friday, a federal court weighed in, ordering the Trump administration to throw out its new rules because HUD didn’t follow proper procedures in making the changes. Applications for the billions in funding were supposed to be due by the end of the month, but the ruling leaves homeless advocates wondering when a new application, and the billions in funding, will be released.

headlines.title: Narcotics operation in San Francisco leads to 87 arrests
headlines.description: A recent narcotics operation in San Francisco led to 87 arrests and the seizure of several pounds of drugs and a few guns, the San Francisco police, district attorney and other agencies announced Friday. “This week we conducted two major enforcement operations. One was focused on arresting outstanding fugitives. In the other we conducted undercover stings that led to the arrests of multiple drug dealers,” San Francisco police Chief Derrik Lew said. Lew also described arrests last week by SFPD in Oakland at four different homes. They said 13 people were arrested on brand new drug and weapons violations, 74 others were arrested who had outstanding warrants or parole violations. Most of these people taken into custody are familiar to officers and prosecutors. In April, the California Supreme Court ruled that only people charged with violent or sexual abuse felonies could be held without bail. These recent arrests come as the San Francisco Police Department continues saturation patrols in the Tenderloin and Mid-Market corridor. Those have been in progress since a series of shootings in the area last month. In one of those incidents, officers who are part of the SFPD’S Narcotics Enforcement Team were among the first to respond to aid the shooting victim and went on to help arrest three people suspected in the incident. The SFPD, sheriff’s department, federal partners and Mayor Daniel Lurie all say these enforcement efforts will continue. “We are doing this every couple of weeks. We have these operations,” Lurie said. “And I want to send a message to everybody, and I want everybody to hear this clearly; if you come to San Francisco to deal drugs or commit crime, we’re going to arrest you, we’re going to prosecute you.” Some of the people arrested this week were arraigned Friday; others will have their first appearance before a judge next Tuesday.

headlines.title: ‘The need is tremendous': Bay Area food banks see longer lines
headlines.description: Bay Area charities are sounding the alarm on a dire situation many families are facing amid higher food prices and cuts to government benefits. Many local nonprofits say there is no light at the end of the tunnel when it comes to trying to meet the demand for food assistance. “The need is tremendous,” said Deborah Dorton, director of a food pantry program at True Vines Baptist Church in San Jose. “There’s a lot of people that are struggling, a lot of people that don’t have enough food. Our crowd is getting bigger and bigger and bigger.” Damian Trujillo takes a closer look at the challenges local charities are facing to help struggling families. Watch his report in the video above. headlines.title: Crews stop forward progress of fire at Garin Regional Park in Hayward
headlines.description: Emergency crews responded late Friday afternoon to a brush fire in Hayward’s Garin Regional Park area. The blaze burned about 15 acres with a moderate rate of spread, according to Cal Fire. Firefighters just after 5 p.m. reported stopping forward progress of the blaze. No other information was immediately available. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: San Jose's Circle of Palms Plaza closed over concerns about dying trees
headlines.description: An iconic landmark in downtown San Jose is closed because of concerns about dying trees. NBC Bay Area cameras were there Friday as city crews fenced off Circle of Palms Plaza, located next to the San Jose Museum of Art. The city said all 32 palm trees in the plaza are in decline, and 15 appear to be dead or dying. To prevent a tree from potentially falling and injuring someone, crews closed the area Friday morning. The city said it will work with a contractor to determine the scope of the damage and develop a timeline for removing the affected trees. Until then, Circle of Palms Plaza will remain closed. The City of San Jose also issued a public safety alert.

headlines.title: Bay Area weekend weather forecast: Hot temperatures and high tides
headlines.description: Heat, fire risk and high tides are converging on the Bay Area this weekend, according to the National Weather Service. Starting Friday and running through Sunday, high temperatures will result in elevated heat risks and a heat advisory for much of the region starting Saturday at 10 a.m. Interior areas of the East Bay will be the hottest, with highs ranging from the upper 90s to low 100s, while South Bay locations will be somewhat cooler with highs in the 80s to lower 90s. Coastal areas will be cooler still with temperatures in the 60s and 70s. “Saturday and Sunday will be the hottest days of this heat advisory period,” said weather service meteorologist Anamaria Navarrete. The heat will be compounded by low humidity levels in the 15% to 30% range that won’t improve much in the overnight hours. During this period, there will be “near critical” fire weather conditions, particularly for higher-elevation areas above the compressed marine layer, like the Diablo, Mayacamas and Santa Lucia mountain ranges. The most concerning fire conditions will happen during the afternoons and evenings, as sea breezes increase after sweltering hot days, according to the weather service. Because wind gusts aren’t currently forecast to peak above 15 mph to 20 mph, however, the risk of fire isn’t expected to increase beyond the “near critical” or “elevated” levels. People who live near the shore or who are heading to those areas to beat the heat should be wary of the marine forecast, which is calling for high tides and localized flooding in some areas. “I want to emphasize the minor coastal flooding that areas along the bay shore and the North Bay will experience, and along the Central Coast,” Navarrete said. “It is going to be hot and people may want to go to the water to cool down.” Beachgoers should be cautious of a robust southern swell coming out of the Pacific Ocean, which isn’t going to be strong enough to warrant a beach hazard statement but will increase the likelihood of sneaker waves and rip currents, she said. Temperatures are expected to drop throughout the region starting Monday.

headlines.title: Electric scooter rider struck, killed in San Francisco, police believe
headlines.description: A person on a stand-up electric scooter died Friday morning after they were struck by the driver of a commercial truck in San Francisco, police believe. The collision happened at about 8:18 a.m. at Powell and Market streets, police said. Responding officers found one person in the street suffering from life-threatening injuries. Emergency personnel tried to save the person, but they died at the scene. “At this time, we believe that the person who was deceased was operating a stand-up electric scooter when a commercial truck involved in the collision struck them,” San Francisco police Officer Robert Rueca said. The truck driver stopped in the area and was cooperating with investigators, police said. Whether the collision would be classified as a hit and run was under investigation. “There is still a lot that we need to uncover,” Rueca said. Anyone with information about the collision is asked to call San Francisco police at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and start the message with SFPD. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Rescued dog who recovered from overly-tight harness ready to be adopted
headlines.description: A Bay Area rescue is giving one young dog a second chance after an unimaginable start to life. Titan, a Husky mix, was seven months old when he was found in a Central Valley shelter with a harness so tight that it had grown into his skin. He was placed on the euthanasia list, but volunteers with Walnut Creek-based Northern California Sled Dog Rescue stepped in to help. “He came into the shelter with a harness that had been put on him when he was smaller than he was when he went into the shelter,” Northern California Sled Dog Rescue volunteer Nancy Curtis said. As Titan grew, the harness did not. It became trapped beneath his skin, causing pain and severe wounds that required emergency treatment. The rescue brought Titan to the Bay Area, where volunteers and veterinarians began months of intensive care. “He required a second surgery to fix some of the complications from that,” Curtis said. “A lot of medications and a lot of healing time.” clear the shelters 13 hours ago clear the shelters Jul 28 clear the shelters Aug 1 Thanks to daily wound care, pain medication and countless hours of help from volunteers, Titan slowly began to heal. His strength returned, and his personality started to shine. “You can’t even tell there was anything wrong with him now,” Curtis said. “He looks fantastic.” Titan’s story is just one of thousands for Northern California Sled Dog Rescue. Since 1998, the nonprofit has specialized in rescuing northern breed dogs — many coming from shelters with nowhere else to go. “We have placed probably over 4,000 dogs into homes since the start of the organization,” Curtis said. Today, the rescue places roughly one to 200 dogs into forever homes each year. It relies on foster families, volunteers and weekend adoption events across the Bay Area to keep the mission going. “We have hundreds of members, dozens of active volunteers,” Curtis said. “We do adoption events almost every weekend around the Bay Area.” Today, Titan is healthy enough to find a forever home. According to the volunteers who know him best, it’s his personality that makes him so special. “Titan has an incredibly sweet, very gentle energy that isn’t necessarily typical of huskies,” Curtis said. “He’s got a really calm, gentle demeanor that I personally find really compelling. I think he’s a really great dog.”

headlines.title: Caltrans reschedules lane closure on Carquinez Bridge
headlines.description: A lane closure previously scheduled for this weekend on the westbound Carquinez Bridge has been rescheduled for the following weekend, according to Caltrans. The one-lane closure on Interstate 80 will take place Aug. 14 at 6 p.m. through Aug. 15 at 7 p.m. Caltrans said in a statement that the closure is due to construction for the agency’s ongoing bridge deck rehabilitation project. A full closure of the westbound Carquinez Bridge is planned for Aug. 21-24. Caltrans is hosting a public meeting to discuss construction plans on Monday at 6 p.m. at the Norman C. King South Vallejo Community Center at 545 Magazine St. in Vallejo. The pedestrian and bike path will remain open during the lane closure. For updates, visit 511.org and quickmap.dot.ca.gov.
